title: Higher-Dimensional Tightness of Gröbner-Basis Lower Bounds
summary: Lower bounds are experimentally tight for small-scale systems, but it remains unresolved whether they stay tight in higher dimensions or what gap separates them from actual solving complexity.

formal_statement.body: For the constructed systems of quadratic equations, lower bounds on Gr?bner-basis solving complexity have been experimentally verified to be tight for small-scale systems, but their tightness in higher dimensions lacks theoretical support. The unresolved task is to determine whether this tightness persists for higher-dimensional instances of the constructed systems or, if it does not, to quantify the gap between each lower bound and the actual solving complexity as system dimension increases.

scope.domain: Algebraic cryptanalysis of symmetric ciphers modeled by overdefined systems of quadratic equations, focusing on Gröbner-basis solving complexity.
parameters: system dimension (the variable along which lower-bound tightness is assessed)
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine whether the tightness persists for higher-dimensional instances of the constructed systems; otherwise, quantify the gap between each lower bound and the actual solving complexity as system dimension increases.

citations.label: Modelling Ciphers with Overdefined Systems of Quadratic Equations: Application to Friday, Vision, RAIN and Biscuit

progress.summary: The source reports experimental verification that the lower bounds are tight for small-scale equation systems, then says the same claim cannot be made for higher dimensions because theoretical support is lacking.
